author: kevaundray
content:
<@&1070471163219824730> / <@&688101493978562687>  / <@&836981603216654336>   -- could you say more about your rationale for 8298?

or more generally, do you see a way in which EOAs will be able to migrate to smart accounts?

author: kevaundray
content: 7702 works in the interim but the EOA is still able to migrate the credentials back in the future, which means in a post PQ world, it would not be an ideal solution

author: draganrakita
content: Imo i want to see how frames add pq support before adding anything else that support pq. SETCODEFROM or ecrecovery precompile nerf, or nuking 7702 etc fall into this bucket.

author: kevaundray
content:
Ah okay, so this would explain your reason for DFIing 8151.

I think outside of PQ, the main reason to do 8298 is that it allows one to permanently retire the EOA "master key"; though I haven't checked how much of an issue this is in practice

author: kevaundray
content: What would you be looking for re frames adding PQ support? (I'm just thinking that maybe in all approaches, we will likely need to upgrade the EOA)

author: daniellehrner
content:
I think the main issue is that SETCODEFROM is irreversible. An attacker tricking a user into setting a malicious contract means the user has lost all their funds without any way to fix that. It does make sense as a cheap way to create clones or proxies though.

EIP-7851 would have made more sense for retiring the ECDSA, but we also only had it in C tier in the Hegota ranking and it was already DFI'd

author: draganrakita
content: Solution needs to be irreversible, as we need to block ecdsa signatures from making changes to account. But seeing first how pq sigs is going to work in parallel with ecdsa and then thinking how to nuke them is imo better flow.
